*Reduced-gravity system designed to inform future lunar landings*


DENVER–(BUSINESS WIRE)–


Voyager Technologies (NYSE: VOYG) announced the successful Phase II testing of their Floatinator system, a reduced-gravity simulator for terrestrial testing of Plume Surface Interaction (PSI) events.


“The plume from lunar landings can be hazardous to spacecraft and equipment, and mitigating these hazards is mission-critical as lunar activity increases,” said John Thornton, executive vice president, Lunar and Space Solutions, Voyager. “With Floatinator, we’re gaining a better understanding of PSI effects that will inform design and concepts for future missions.”


PSI testing is difficult to conduct on Earth due to Earth’s gravity and atmosphere. Floatinator is designed to address gaps in current data sets, generating a better understanding of PSI to inform engine design and landing operations, increasing the likelihood of successful lunar landings. Initial Phase I testing proved out the system’s core capabilities, and Phase II took it further with a full-size Floatinator for faster acceleration and increased travel distances to better simulate a lunar landing. This phase of the test uses cold gas thrusters, gives more precise control of the acceleration rate and collects data at multiple gravity levels.


During the test, a 350-pound payload sled was dropped from a 35-foot structure using a controlled acceleration profile to simulate lunar gravity. During the drop, a cold gas thruster fired into a regolith bin to simulate the effects of a lunar landing. The team collected data with high-speed cameras, accelerometers and flow meters. Test results will be reported to NASA for inclusion in their modeling ahead of a similar planned NASA study — Stereo Cameras for Lunar Plume-Surface Studies (SCALPSS) — to be conducted during Voyager’s future lunar landing missions.


Voyager is building the infrastructure that will make America’s permanent presence on the Moon a reality. With the most fully integrated commercial lunar platform, the company has the capability at every layer required to land on the lunar surface, sustain life and execute critical missions.
